  • Named in 1695 for Princess Anne (1665-1714), who became heiress apparent in December 1694 upon the death of her sister, Queen Mary II of England, Scotland, and Ireland. As Queen Anne, she ascended the throne in 1702 following the death of Mary's husband, King William III. In 1707, England and Scotland united and Anne became Queen of Great Britain and Ireland, which she ruled until her death.
    • State Capital of Maryland, County Seat of Anne Arundel County (formerly Anne Arundel Town)
    • Population
      1990 census: 33,195
      2000 census: 35,838
      2010 census: 38,394
      2020 census: 40,812
    • Reports
